transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{Linear relationships}}\par\text{ Examples include a fixed salary plus commission, temperature conversions and simple altitude–temperature models.}
\text{\textbf{Arithmetic sequences}}\par\text{ The sequence 2,5,8,11,14 has constant difference 3. Its nth term is \(3n-1\), a linear expression.}
\text{Look for a constant absolute change. Real data may only be approximately linear; specify the range where a model is reasonable.}

sourceMapping.method: Source-checked native text and LaTeX; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{A straight-line model}}\par\text{ Plot paired GCSE and A level marks on a scatter diagram. A line of best fit can describe an approximate relationship.}
\text{\textbf{Interpret the parameters}}\par\text{ The gradient estimates the change in predicted A level mark per extra GCSE mark. The intercept is the prediction when the GCSE mark is zero.}
\text{The intercept may have no practical meaning if zero lies far outside the data. Predictions are estimates; extrapolation beyond the observed range is less reliable.}
